title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs
seoTitle: Paris living costs and school funding protests

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated over school funding shortages, rising living costs, and general economic conditions in France.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded better school funding, improved staffing, higher wages, and higher pensions.
tea.changed: Oct 25: Clashes broke out during nationwide demonstrations, resulting in numerous arrests and injuries.

summary: Demonstrations involving hundreds of thousands of people took place across France, including Paris, to protest against the high cost of living, inadequate school funding, and staff shortages. The marches, which began peacefully, saw clashes near their endpoints where some participants threw projectiles and fireworks, and police responded with tear gas, water cannons, and sound grenades. The Interior Ministry and the CGT union reported differing turnout figures, while authorities deployed heavy security forces nationwide. The unrest led to numerous arrests, property damage, and injuries among both protesters and police officers. President Emmanuel Macron and other officials condemned the violence, warning that those responsible for destroying property and attacking authorities would be prosecuted.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez deployed up to 70,000 officers backed by water cannons and armored vehicles. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence and promised that those who caused destruction and chaos would be prosecuted and punished.

crowd.text: The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000

arrests.text: Nationally, according to authorities, arrests have exceeded 1,200

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Clashes erupted in Paris and across France as demonstrations drew hundreds of thousands of participants.
The French retail chamber reported severe business losses and damage to thousands of shops during the protests.
